title: Navigational sprint grid for Q3 hosted API + model catalog commitments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight, reusable planning artifact — the 'Navigational Sprint Grid' — to map quarterly OKRs and initiative lanes to concrete sprint commitments for the Hosted API + Model Catalog domain. The goal is to reduce ambiguity when committing model rotations, canary windows, and cross-team capacity hedges so that PMs, Eng, and Design can make clean handoffs and automated rollout schedules.

Background: Previous quarterly plans have been long-form and narrative-heavy; engineering reported difficulty translating them into per-sprint work that respects Dedicated capacity hedges and runtime gating. This ticket creates a single-source artifact that translates OKRs into prioritized lanes (Critical, Improve Cost, Health & Reliability, Experiments) with explicit decision gates, canary windows, and telemetry requirements.

Scope: Create the grid template, run a pilot mapping for Q3 hosted-model rotations (top 8 models by traffic), and produce the sprint-by-sprint commitments (+ fallthrough plan) for the first two sprints of the quarter. Deliverables: 1) grid template in Confluence, 2) completed Q3 grid with owners and canary windows, 3) PRD summarizing rollout rules and risk thresholds, 4) two-week cadence handoff checklist for Eng & Console teams.

Non-goals: Not implementing runtime changes — implementation work remains owned by engineering tickets. This is a planning/product artifact and playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence grid template published and linked from roadmap page
Top-8 hosted models mapped into lanes with primary/secondary owners
Canary windows and fallback rules documented for each model (duration, metrics, rollback thresholds)
Runbook for cross-team handoff (PM -> Eng -> Console) authored and reviewed
Pilot sprint commitments for first two sprints created and assigned in Linear
